scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: host_1_1_1_1 default-gateway configuration
Mechanism: host_1_1_1_1's correct gateway is 10.1.1.1 (switch_dist_1_1's br0
  address). Its default route was repointed to 10.1.1.254 -- in-subnet but
  unassigned -- so ARP for the gateway never resolves and no off-subnet
  packet leaves the host. On-link destinations (10.1.1.1 via the connected
  route) still work, which is why the gateway pings fine. DNS "times out"
  only because the resolver 10.200.0.2 is off-subnet. The network itself is
  healthy: pod 2 reaches everything, and switch_dist_1_1 still advertises
  10.1.1.0/24.
Localization: host_1_1_1_1
Root cause: host_1_1_1_1's default gateway set to 10.1.1.254 instead of
  10.1.1.1
Fix: restore the default route on host_1_1_1_1 --
  `ip route replace default via 10.1.1.1 dev eth0`
scenario.fix_spec:
restore host_1_1_1_1's default route --
`ip route replace default via 10.1.1.1 dev eth0`
scoring_axes: must-identify-component: default gateway / default route points at wrong address (10.1.1.254 instead of 10.1.1.1)
bonus-exonerates-network: notes switch_dist_1_1 and the OSPF core are healthy (pod 2 works, the real gateway answers), so no network device needs fixing

agent.diagnosis_text:
Affected component: host routing configuration on host_1_1_1_1. The host’s default gateway is misconfigured to 10.1.1.254, which does not exist on the subnet.

Mechanism: For any destination outside 10.1.1.0/24, the host forwards to its default next-hop 10.1.1.254. ARP resolution for that next-hop fails, so the kernel immediately returns “Destination Host Unreachable,” causing all off-subnet traffic (including DNS to 10.200.0.2 and other pods) to fail. Local-subnet traffic (e.g., to 10.1.1.1) still works, explaining why the gateway IP is pingable.

Localization and evidence:
- host_1_1_1_1 ip route: “default via 10.1.1.254 dev eth0”
- host_1_1_1_1 ARP: “10.1.1.254 FAILED”; pings to off-subnets return “From 10.1.1.2 Destination Host Unreachable”
- host_1_1_1_1 can ping 10.1.1.1
- switch_dist_1_1 (the VLAN SVI) has br0 at 10.1.1.1/24 and OSPF-learned routes to 10.2.1.0/24 and 10.200.0.0/24, confirming upstream routing is healthy
- host_2_1_1_1, on a different subnet, reaches everything normally with default via 10.2.1.1

Root cause: The default gateway on host_1_1_1_1 is set to a non-existent next-hop (10.1.1.254) instead of the correct SVI 10.1.1.1.

Corrective fix: Change host_1_1_1_1’s default route to “default via 10.1.1.1 dev eth0,” removing the 10.1.1.254 entry. Make this persistent in the host’s network config (e.g., netplan or /etc/network/interfaces) or correct DHCP option 3 if DHCP-configured. Flush any stale ARP/route entries and retest reachability (ping 10.200.0.2, 10.2.1.2; DNS lookups).

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly identifies host_1_1_1_1 as the affected device and attributes the issue to its host-side routing configuration.
